output.name: Keret — The Pole-Runner
output.myth: Keret is the tern who runs from pole to pole and back each year. Hesk counts the birds at the pole and says one is missing. Tavo the Gale pushed Keret off course in autumn, and the people grieved at the cliff, burned a little smoke, and mended her nets for no one. Then, in the dead of winter, a wet shape comes over the headland. Nethe the Drying Shag, on the black rock to the north, who has never once gone in the water, watched her come and said nothing. Keret lands on the wrong stake, shakes salt over the hearth, and asks whether any fish is left. The Gulls shriek the news across Vel. Nobody had said she was dead, only late. Aun laughed at that, since Aun is always late too. Harel the Bone Gull, south-west of her, hangs on a string to Hesk's reel and cannot come down to meet her. So if you are lost, do not be ashamed to come home wet. Hesk will keep your place on the Spindle, and Keret will tell you where the wind went.
output.finding: Find the Drying Shag, Nethe, on the black rock under the Windward cliffs, and Keret lies about two-thirds of a hand-span due south of it.
